It's based on libFuzzer and provides native Python fuzzing with coverage instrumentation.\n\n## Installation\n\n```bash\npip install atheris\n```\n\nFor better coverage instrumentation, also install:\n```bash\npip install coverage\n```\n\n## Basic Fuzz Driver Structure\n\n```python\n#!/usr/bin/env python3\nimport atheris\nimport sys\n\n# Import the library to test\n# import target_library\n\ndef TestOneInput(data: bytes) -> None:\n    \"\"\"\n    The fuzzing entry point. Takes arbitrary bytes as input.\n\n    Args:\n        data: Raw bytes from the fuzzer\n    \"\"\"\n    if len(data) < 1:\n        return\n\n    try:\n        # Convert bytes to useful format\n        # Option 1: Decode as string\n        text = data.decode('utf-8', errors='ignore')\n\n        # Option 2: Use FuzzedDataProvider for structured data\n        fdp = atheris.FuzzedDataProvider(data)\n        string_val = fdp.ConsumeUnicodeNoSurrogates(100)\n        int_val = fdp.ConsumeIntInRange(0, 1000)\n        bool_val = fdp.ConsumeBool()\n\n        # Call target function\n        # atheris.Fuzz()\n\nif __name__ == \"__main__\":\n    main()\n```\n\n## FuzzedDataProvider Methods\n\n```python\nfdp = atheris.FuzzedDataProvider(data)\n\n# String methods\nfdp.ConsumeString(max_length)           # ASCII string\nfdp.ConsumeUnicode(max_length)          # Unicode string (may have surrogates)\nfdp.ConsumeUnicodeNoSurrogates(max_length)  # Safe unicode\n\n# Integer methods\nfdp.ConsumeInt(num_bytes)               # Integer from bytes\nfdp.ConsumeIntInRange(min, max)         # Integer in range\nfdp.ConsumeIntList(max_count, num_bytes)  # List of integers\n\n# Float methods\nfdp.ConsumeFloat()                      # Float in [0, 1]\nfdp.ConsumeFloatInRange(min, max)       # Float in range\nfdp.ConsumeRegularFloat()               # Regular float (no special \"package1>=1.0\",\n        \"package2\"\n    ],\n    extras_require={\n        \"dev\": [\"pytest\", \"black\"],\n        \"test\": [\"pytest\", \"coverage\"]\n    }\n)\n```\n\n## Finding Check Package Structure\n\n```bash\n# Find main package directory\nls -la\nfind . -name \"__init__.py\" | head -20\n\n# Identify main modules\nfind . -name \"*.py\" -path \"*/src/*\" -o -name \"*.py\" -path \"*/<package_name>/*\"\n```\n\n### 2. Look at Public API\n\nCheck these files for exported functions:\n- `__init__.py` - Exports via `__all__`\n- `api.py` or `public.py` - Public interface\n- Documentation files\n\n```python\n# In __init__.py\n__all__ = ['parse', 'load', 'dump']  # These are the main APIs\n```\n\n### 3. Check Type Annotations\n\n```python\ndef parse(data: str) -> Result:  # Takes string input\ndef load(fp: BinaryIO) -> Data:  # Takes file-like object\ndef decode(raw: bytes) -> Output:  # Takes bytes\n```\n\n## Common Library Patterns\n\n### Data Serialization Libraries (ujson, orjson)\n```python\n# Target functions\nlib.loads(string)      # Parse from string\nlib.load(file)         # Parse from file\nlib.dumps(obj)         # Serialize to string\nlib.dump(obj, file)    # Serialize to file\n```\n\n### Date/Time Libraries (arrow, dateutil)\n```python\n# Target functions\nlib.get(string)        # Parse date string\nlib.parse(string)      # Parse with format\nlib.Arrow.fromtimestamp(ts)  # From timestamp\n```\n\n### Code Formatters (black, autopep8)\n```python\n# Target functions\nlib.format_str(code, mode)  # Format code string\nlib.format_file(path)       # Format file\n```\n\n### REPL/Shell Libraries (ipython)\n```python\n# Target functions\nlib.run_cell(code)     # Execute code\nlib.parse(code)        # Parse code\nlib.transform(code)    # Transform code\n```\n\n## Analysis Checklist\n\n1. **Package structure**: Identify main module and submodules\n2. **Public API**: Find exported functions in `__init__.py`\n3. **Input types**: Note what types each function accepts\n4. **Exception handling**: Identify expected vs unexpected exceptions\n5. **Dependencies**: Check what other libraries are used\n6. **Tests**: Look at test files for usage examples\n\n## Sample Notes Format\n\n```markdown\n# Library: example-lib\n\n## Main Entry Points\n- `example_lib.parse(data: str) -> Result` - 464→        # Any number of S is the same as one.\n   465→        # TODO: allow users to specify the number of digits to parse\n   466→        escaped_fmt = re.sub(r\"S+\", \"S\", escaped_fmt)\n
